title: Scrutinizing Variables for Checkpoint Using Automatic Differentiation
problem: Checkpointing stores entire variables including elements that have no impact on application output, wasting storage resources. Current checkpoint methods do not distinguish between critical and uncritical elements within variables.
motivation: Reducing checkpoint storage overhead is critical for large-scale HPC applications that rely on periodic checkpointing for fault tolerance and iterative computation.
method: Programs save memory snapshots called checkpoints to enable fast recomputation, but currently save every element in a variable even if some don't affect the result. This method uses automatic differentiation—which traces how changes in input values propagate through calculations—to identify which elements of each variable actually influence the final output. It then stores only these critical elements, omitting the rest.
key_novelty: By using automatic differentiation to distinguish which individual data elements impact the program's output, checkpoints can be optimized to save only the critical elements.
contributions: Systematic AD-based methodology for element-level checkpoint analysis and criticality assessment
Technique to identify and eliminate uncritical elements from checkpoint storage
Comprehensive validation across NAS Parallel Benchmark suite with critical/uncritical element distribution visualization
Demonstration of up to 19% checkpoint storage savings in practice
